correctness.rationale: The exact two-channel determinant in Arutkin–Vallée §III.2 is an explicitly identified source premise. Its division by \(\alpha\) yields the rational inverse \(G(q)\), with positive factors on the physical interval. The logarithmic derivative proves \(G'(q)>0\); polynomial division independently gives \(G''(q)=2d_\ell d_h/\bar d+2\bar d^2R/(J-\bar d q)^3>0\), with \(R>0\). Inverse differentiation establishes \(\alpha'(\mu)>0\) and \(\alpha''(\mu)<0\). Endpoint expansions derive from a simple numerator zero at \(J/d_h\) and simple denominator zero at \(J/\bar d\), yielding \(\beta/(J+d_h)\) and the variance-weighted coefficient \(K\). A separate standard-library checker ran 485 exact-rational parameter cases verifying determinant substitution, quotient and partial-fraction curvature, and both endpoint coefficients. These finite checks supplement the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For the already-motivated two-state fluctuating-volatility model, the latent redraw rate is not directly observable but the stationary Pareto exponent is empirically meaningful. An exact one-to-one inverse determines whether one tail index can identify one refresh rate conditional on other known parameters; strict concavity provides a parameter-uniform law of diminishing returns, rather than a local plot-based inference. The sharp slow-refresh slope \(\beta/(J+d_h)\) and fast-refresh coefficient proportional to \(\beta(1-\beta)(d_h-d_\ell)^2\) quantify experimentally relevant sensitivity and loss of identifiability at fast refresh. It is a coherent structural classification on a natural whole parameter domain, not an arbitrary numerical slice. It claims neither finite-sample estimation guarantees nor a broad new wealth-model framework.
